title: Coherent relative co-Yoneda density and extension
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent mapping spaces, functor categories and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small ordinary category $I$, and infinity categories $\mathcal B,\mathcal E$ admitting all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, formed in larger universes when necessary. No presentability or local smallness relative to $\mathcal U$ is assumed. Put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal B)$. This category has $\mathcal U$-small colimits, computed pointwise, and evaluation preserves them. The coherent free diagram $i!x$ is defined by $(i!x)(j)=\coprod_{\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)}x$, with structure maps induced by composition in $I$. It is contravariantly functorial in $i$ and covariantly functorial in $x$, and there are coherent natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(i!x,F)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,F(i)).$$
Every $F$ has the canonical co-Yoneda colimit presentation by the free diagrams equipped with maps to $F$:
$$F\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{(i,x,a:x\to F(i))} i!x.$$
Precisely, the indexing category is the relative slice of $N(I)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal P$, $(i,x)\mapsto i!x$, over $F$; although this slice may be large, it admits a final map from a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $K_F$. Here a map to an indexing infinity category is final when restricting along it leaves the colimit of every coherent diagram unchanged, in every target universe in which those colimits exist. The displayed colimit and cocone can therefore be computed on $K_F$. Mapping out of this colimit gives the corresponding limit of mapping spaces, in a universe containing those spaces.

Write $\operatorname{Fun}^L_{\mathcal U}$ for the full coherent functor subcategory on functors preserving $\mathcal U$-small colimits. Restriction along $(i,x)\mapsto i!x$ induces an equivalence between $\operatorname{Fun}^L_{\mathcal U}(\mathcal P,\mathcal E)$ and the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(I)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B,\mathcal E)$ on $T$ for which each $T(i,-)$ preserves $\mathcal U$-small colimits. The extension $H_T$ sends $F$ to the colimit of $T(i,x)$ on the same $K_F$, and satisfies $H_T(i!x)\simeq T(i,x)$ coherently. Restriction is an equivalence on entire functor categories, including transformations; in particular natural transformations between colimit-preserving extensions are determined by their restrictions to the free diagrams.

source.place: Section 6.7: relative Yoneda formulas (6.7.1.1)-(6.7.1.3), Theorem 6.7.2, Lemma 6.7.5 and Lemma 6.7.7, printed pp. 315-318, with A=N(I)^op. Pointwise colimits are the dual of Theorem 6.1.22. The small final map is the explicit interpretation in the proof of Theorem 7.9.8 following (7.9.8.10), printed pp. 410-411. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical relative co-Yoneda theorem.

proof.text: For every $\mathcal U$-small simplicial shape $L$, existence of its colimits in $\mathcal B$ says exactly that each diagram has a universal arrow to the constant-diagram functor $\Delta_L:\mathcal B\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal B)$. The opposite form of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] assembles these arrows into $\operatorname{colim}_L\dashv\Delta_L$, with its adjunction on functor categories with any simplicial parameters. Apply this parametrized adjunction with parameter $N(I)$ and use the canonical currying isomorphism (interchanging the two parameter factors) $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal B))\cong\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal B))$. The left adjoint to the constant-$L$ functor on $\mathcal P$ is therefore postcomposition with $\operatorname{colim}_L$; its unit evaluated at $j$ is the original colimit unit in $\mathcal B$. This constructs the pointwise colimit cocones. The cocone criterion and componentwise equivalence detection of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] show that a specified cocone is colimiting exactly when all its evaluations are: compare it to the constructed cocone and test the resulting map componentwise. In particular, evaluations preserve these colimits. For any further simplicial parameter $M$, apply the cited parametrized adjunction to $M\times N(I)$: the degreewise product permutation and currying identify its unit at $(m,j)$ with the original colimit unit in $\mathcal B$. Restriction along $M^\prime\to M$ commutes with that product permutation and unit. Thus the pointwise cocones and their comparisons retain all simplicial parameters, in any containing universe.

source.place: Corollary 6.2.10, printed p. 279, dualized; its parametrized-adjunction input is Theorem 6.1.22.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-ordinary-pointwise-kan-extension] to the ordinary functor $\{*\}\to I$ with value $i$ (it need not be full when $i$ has endomorphisms). Its comma category over $j$ is the discrete set $\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)$. The pointwise formula gives $i!x(j)=\coprod_{i\to j}x$, with composition structure maps and the coherent adjunction $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(i!x,F)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,F(i))$. For $v:i\to i'$, the comma-map clause gives $i'!x\to i!x$ by sending the summand $w:i'\to j$ to $wv:i\to j$. Its coherent compatibility with composition makes $Q:N(I)^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal P$, $Q(i,x)=i!x$, a functor, including all higher parameters. The adjunction is natural in all three variables, and its counit sends the $w$ summand by $F(w)$. Each $i!$ preserves $\mathcal U$-small colimits: the parametrized adjunction identifies cocones from $i!$ of a diagram with cocones from that diagram after evaluation, so the colimit universal arrow is preserved.

source.place: Relative Yoneda formula (6.7.1.1); the ordinary comma-category specialization of Proposition 6.4.9.

proof.text: Put $A=N(I)$, $D=A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B$ and $K=\operatorname{Tw}(A)^{\mathrm{op}}=N(\operatorname{Tw}(I)^{\mathrm{op}})$. For $u:a\to b$ put $d_F(u)=(b,F(a))$. An arrow $u\to u'$ in $\operatorname{Tw}(I)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a pair $f:a\to a'$, $g:b'\to b$ with $u=gu'f$; its image uses $(g,F(f))$. Thus $d_F$ is the composite of a fixed endpoint projection with evaluation, retaining the higher simplices of $F$. Its free-diagram cocone to $F$ has leg adjoint to $F(u):F(a)\to F(b)$. To prove that this actual map $K\to D_{/F}$ is final, the opposite of the relative slice $D_{/F}:=D\times_{\mathcal P}\mathcal P_{/F}$ is a left fibration over $D^{\mathrm{op}}=A\times\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. The slice and twisted-arrow statements identify its classifier as $(i,x)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(Q(i,x),F)$. Step 2 identifies this coherently with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,F(i))$. By space-valued straightening and the classifier clause of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-graph-cofinality], this is exactly $W_F$, with the product factors interchanged. Under this equivalence the opposite of our cocone map is $\kappa_F$, since its leg is $F(u)$, not merely a map with the same endpoints. The graph theorem therefore proves finality in every containing universe. The fixed $K$ is $\mathcal U$-small and serves as $K_F$ for every $F$; no smallness of mapping spaces relative to $\mathcal U$ was used.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.5 and Proposition 5.6.9, second graph map; interpretation after (7.9.8.10).

proof.text: We will flatten coproducts by the following calculation, rather than assume an interchange theorem for varying sets. For a $\mathcal U$-small ordinary category $C_0$ and functor $S:C_0\to\mathrm{Set}_{\mathcal U}$, let $E_S$ have objects $(c,s\in S(c))$ and arrows $r:c\to c'$ with $S(r)s=s'$, and let $p:E_S\to C_0$ be projection. In $(p\downarrow c)$, the full subcategory consisting of $((c,s),1_c)$ is discrete and its inclusion is right adjoint to $((b,t),r)\mapsto S(r)t$: there is exactly one map to $((c,s),1_c)$ when $S(r)t=s$. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-adjoint-reindexing] this inclusion does not change colimit cocones. The pointwise Kan formula consequently gives $(p_!V)(c)=\coprod_{s\in S(c)}V(c,s)$ for every coherent $V:N(E_S)\to\mathcal B$. Composing the adjunctions $p_!\dashv p^*$ and $\operatorname{colim}_{C_0}\dashv\Delta_{C_0}$ identifies $\operatorname{colim}_{C_0}p_!V$ with $\operatorname{colim}_{E_S}V$: both have the same mapping-space adjunction to $\Delta_{E_S}$. The identifications use the specified colimit legs and are coherent with arbitrary parameters by the parametrized adjunctions. This calculation applies with $\mathcal E$ in place of $\mathcal B$ as well.

source.place: Agent comma-category calculation from Proposition 6.4.9; used to compute the relative Yoneda cocone of Lemma 6.7.7.

proof.text: Evaluate the cocone of step 3 at $j\in I$. Step 4 identifies its source colimit with the colimit of $F(a)$ on the ordinary category $L_j$ of pairs $(u:a\to b,w:b\to j)$; an arrow to $(u':a'\to b',w')$ is $(f:a\to a',g:b'\to b)$ with $u=gu'f$ and $w'=wg$. Define $p_j:L_j\to I_{/j}$ by $(u,w)\mapsto wu$, and define $s_j:I_{/j}\to L_j$ by $t:a\to j\mapsto(t,1_j)$. There are natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{L_j}(s_j(t),(u,w))=\{f\mid t=wuf\}=\operatorname{Hom}_{I_{/j}}(t,p_j(u,w))$; thus $s_j\dashv p_j$. The diagram $F(a)$ factors through $p_j$, which is final by right-adjoint reindexing. The category $I_{/j}$ has terminal object $1_j$, so its colimit is $F(j)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit]. The resulting leg on $(u,w)$ is precisely $F(wu)$, the evaluation of the cocone already specified in step 3. Consequently that specified cocone is pointwise colimiting, hence is colimiting in $\mathcal P$ by step 1. Together with finality in step 3 this proves the asserted large-relative-slice presentation.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.7, with the density calculation expanded by ordinary slice adjunctions.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal T$ be the full functor subcategory in the statement. Define a coherent diagram depending on $(T,F)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal P$ by $u:a\to b\mapsto T(b,F(a))$, using the same fixed projection from $K$ as in step 3 and the evaluation functors for $T$ and $F$. Compose its curried functor with $\operatorname{colim}_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal E$ to obtain $S(T)=H_T$. This is a functor on $\mathcal T$, including transformations and higher simplices, because it is a composite of coherent evaluation, currying and the colimit functor, rather than an assembly of independently chosen objects. Each $F\mapsto T(b,F(a))$ preserves $\mathcal U$-small colimits by step 1 and the hypothesis on $T(b,-)$. The colimit functor $\operatorname{colim}_K$ preserves these colimits: it is a left adjoint by step 1, and the parametrized adjunction carries a pointwise colimit cocone to the universal cocone for its image. Equivalently, for any $\mathcal U$-small shape $L$, the two iterated colimit functors on $\operatorname{Fun}(L\times K,\mathcal E)$ are left adjoint to the same doubly constant functor. Their universal-arrow equivalence identifies their cocone legs, giving the required interchange. Hence $H_T$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits. Restriction $R(H)=HQ$ lands in $\mathcal T$ since each $i!$ preserves these colimits by step 2.

source.place: Construction in Theorem 6.7.2 and Lemma 6.7.7; pointwise-colimit argument of Proposition 6.3.12.

proof.text: For a free diagram $i!x$, the formula for $S$ gives $S(T)(i!x)=\operatorname{colim}_{u:a\to b}\,T(b,\coprod_{v:i\to a}x)$. Since $T(b,-)$ preserves coproducts, this is $\operatorname{colim}_{u}\coprod_{v:i\to a}T(b,x)$. The comparison is canonical: it is induced by the coproduct injections under $T(b,-)$, so it is coherent also in $b$ and $T$. Step 4 flattens it to the category $J_i$ of pairs $(u:a\to b,v:i\to a)$, with arrows $(f:a\to a',g:b'\to b)$ satisfying $u=gu'f$ and $v'=fv$. Define $p_i:J_i\to(i/I)^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $(u,v)\mapsto uv:i\to b$ and $s_i:(i/I)^{\mathrm{op}}\to J_i$ by $w:i\to c\mapsto(w,1_i)$. A map $s_i(w)\to(u,v)$ has its $f$ forced to be $v$, and its remaining datum is $g:b\to c$ with $w=guv$. These are exactly the maps $w\to uv$ in $(i/I)^{\mathrm{op}}$, proving $s_i\dashv p_i$. The diagram on $J_i$ is the pullback of $w:i\to b\mapsto T(b,x)$, and $p_i$ is final by right-adjoint reindexing. Since $1_i$ is terminal in $(i/I)^{\mathrm{op}}$, its colimit is $T(i,x)$. The resulting equivalence $S(T)(i!x)\to T(i,x)$ uses $T(uv):T(b,x)\to T(i,x)$ on each summand. For $h:i'\to i$, precomposing $v$ by $h$ changes this leg to $T(uvh)=T(h)T(uv)$, with the composition coherences supplied by $T$ itself. A map or higher simplex in $x$ or $T$ is sent through the same evaluation and colimit functors. Thus these comparisons define the coherent natural equivalence $RS\simeq1_{\mathcal T}$, including all parameters.

source.place: Free-diagram calculation for Theorem 6.7.2; two explicit slice adjunctions replace an appeal to abstract relative completion.

proof.text: For every colimit-preserving $H:\mathcal P\to\mathcal E$, the density cocone of step 5 induces a comparison $S(R(H))(F)=\operatorname{colim}_{u:a\to b}H(b!F(a))\to H(F)$. It is an equivalence because $K$ is $\mathcal U$-small and $H$ preserves its colimit. The density cocone was defined by the adjunction counit and the evaluation functor on all $(u,F)$ in step 3. Applying evaluation on $(H,F)$ and then the colimit functor therefore gives this comparison as a coherent natural transformation on the entire functor subcategory, including every higher simplex. Componentwise equivalence detection makes it a natural equivalence $SR\simeq1$. Along with $RS\simeq1$ from step 7, these are quasi-inverse functors between the two full quasicategories in the statement. This proves the equivalence on entire functor categories, so in particular the restriction on spaces of transformations is an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 6.7.2, inverse equivalences constructed directly from the density cocone.

proof.text: For completeness, the mapping-out assertion retains the whole limit of spaces. For a diagram $V:K\to\mathcal P$ and $G\in\mathcal P$, pull back $\mathcal P_{/G}\to\mathcal P$ along $V$. This is a right fibration, and the twisted-arrow slice comparison and mapping-space classifier identify it with the right fibration classified by $m:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$, $m(k)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(V(k),G)$, in a sufficiently large universe. Its space of sections is the space of coherent cocones from $V$ to $G$: the join/fat-cone comparison identifies both models with the fixed-boundary, fixed-vertex cocone space. Under the opposite of space-valued straightening, maps from a space $X$ to this section space are maps of right fibrations $X\times K\to K\times_{\mathcal P}\mathcal P_{/G}$, equivalently coherent transformations $\Delta X\to m$. This is precisely the mapping-space universal property of $\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}m$; the section space is Kan because, under straightening, it is the mapping space from the terminal constant presheaf to $m$. The colimit cocone of step 5 identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(F,G)$ with that cocone space by the colimit criterion. It therefore gives the claimed limit formula. Finality in step 3 permits either the small index or the full relative slice, with the latter interpreted in an ambient universe containing it.

source.place: Mapping-space form of Lemma 6.7.7 and the calculation after (7.9.8.10); section-space verification of the limit universal property.

proof.text: If $I$ is empty, $K$ is empty and $\mathcal P$ is terminal. A colimit-preserving functor from it selects an initial object of $\mathcal E$, whose space of choices is contractible by the cone criterion; $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,\mathcal E)$ is terminal, as required. If $I=*$, $K=*$ and the formulas are $Q(*,x)=x$ and $H_T(F)=T(*,F)$. For discrete $I$, $K$ is discrete and $H_T(F)=\coprod_iT(i,F(i))$. For $I=[1]$, $K$ is the span $1_0\leftarrow(0\to1)\to1_1$, and the formula is the pushout $T(0,F(0))\amalg_{T(1,F(0))}T(1,F(1))$ with the first map coming from contravariance in $I$. Empty coproducts and an initial $x$ give initial free diagrams and initial extension values, since the functors preserve the empty colimit. These checks require no nonzero objects or field hypotheses.

source.place: Agent edge-case and variance checks of the formulas; no claim of compatibility with arbitrary change of I is used.
